topics.caution: The explanation or real_life_example could lean on the common comic stereotype of વાણિયો as timid or miserly, which this very poem overturns by showing ધૂળો as brave and quick-witted.
topics.guidance: In the explanation, name વાણિયો simply as ધૂળાનો વ્યવસાય (a trader) and let the story's own point — his હિંમત — carry the identity, without adding a caste joke the text does not make.

topics.caution: The explanation or real_life_example could present ધૂળાનું 'કોથળો વીંઝે સબોસબ' (swinging his કાટલાં-ભરેલો કોથળો at the thieves) as a fighting move for a child to try out, and it could dwell on 'ઘાવ' (blows) as the point of the scene rather than on his ચતુરાઈ; the block 12 નાટ્યીકરણ activity could turn 'સબોસબ'/'ધબોધબ' into an actual swung prop during class dramatization.
topics.guidance: Keep the explanation on ધૂળાની ચતુરાઈ — using what was already in hand, and how he ખાળે ઘાવ (kept himself from being hit) — never as a technique to copy; the guidance for the block 12 dramatization should tell the teacher to mime the સબોસબ/ધબોધબ action with no real swinging of a bag or any object at another child.

topics.caution: 'ધૂળો ખેલે જંગ' and 'રંગ બતાવવો' could be explained as literal warfare or glorified combat rather than the poem's idiom for holding his ground with confidence.
topics.guidance: Gloss 'જંગ ખેલે' and 'રંગ બતાવવો' as idioms for ધૂળાનો હિંમતભર્યો સામનો (standing his ground bravely), keeping the register as courage, not violence.

chapter_level.guidance: For block 12 (નાટ્યીકરણ) and block 13 (સમૂહગાન), any staged re-enactment of the ચોર-ધૂળો encounter should stay mimed and spoken — no real striking, no real bag-swinging, no real props used to hit another child; block 13's group singing itself carries no safety concern.
